reviewType: Independent read-only source review plus inspection of existing parent development evidence. Reviewer did not execute tests, MCP, native/helper, GUI, builds or edit source.
scope: Host options.meta forwarding in stdio/HTTP MCP clients, actual FastMCP request-context metadata extraction, ACC request/tool journal scopes, batch child context, independent metadata-only receipt reader, and real-stdio qualification source.
implementationState: Uncommitted full execution-receipts WIP. The development harness supplies host transport metadata; normal provider direct/proxy workflow durable preparation and metadata activation are not yet integrated.
outcome: No new actionable source finding identified in this reviewed context slice. Previously noted SDK-interface fallback and JSON-clone shape issues have been addressed in the reviewed current source.
checked: Both JS MCP transports call the same host-only metadata builder, preserving params.arguments separately from params._meta. The cloned result is revalidated as an object after JSON serialization, including toJSON replacement cases.

PlatformMCP reads the SDK request context rather than model arguments. Missing old SDK get_context/request_context/meta interfaces retain a legacy path; a separate capability value probes installed interface shape and extended Meta preservation.
Reserved metadata namespace, exact fields, schema, random invocation identity, bounded session/turn identifiers and hash/codec shapes are checked. Metadata supplies no path or authorization.
ACC accepted arguments are snapshotted before SDK parameter coercion; registered wrapper entry binds the actual arguments and applies defaults before storing a separate snapshot.
The current wrapper was actually invoked when tool_entered is generated; that stage is registered-wrapper entry, not proof of application consumption or native effects.
Batch direct tool.fn calls pass through registered receipt wrappers. Each child has its own operation ID, parent operation and step context; prevalidation refusals do not manufacture child entries.
Request, operation and batch ContextVars reset in finally. Existing raw-thread copy_context supplies propagation for input_sequence.
Native adapter and journal stages remain linked to the actual child operation. Existing native typed terminal validation and entry-before-continue barriers are reused.

SDK request completion is recorded separately from tool result flags. A returned failed macro can have acc_request_terminal ok=true while tool_terminal ok=false; these facts must not be folded into tool success.
execution_receipt exposes bounded committed metadata and references, not private argument blobs; missing/incomplete evidence does not become success merely because the read tool executed.

runs.change: Adds metadata_transport_supported=true assertion to the existing receipt check.

developmentEvidenceObserved.operations: wait and get_mouse_position/mouse.position only; actual MCP stdio and SDK, no fixture injection of ContextVars.
developmentEvidenceObserved.limits: These are existing parent development runs, not new independent runtime acceptance or whole P5 acceptance.

mandatoryFollowUps: caller_args_sha256 currently remains a caller declaration whose shape is checked. Its separate actual received-argument snapshot uses a different codec. Before Node reconciliation claims argument equality, define and verify a cross-codec/canonical binding; matching only the echoed caller hash is insufficient.

metadata_transport_supported is an SDK-interface/shape capability probe, not an ACK for a particular call. Future Node enablement should establish a safe real metadata probe and receipt association, then independently validate each invocation receipt.
Node durable preparation, direct/proxy activation, returned-result persistence and restart reconciliation remain unimplemented.

Strict reader per-stage field/transition and argument-reference semantics, retention/global-space management, single-request capture/OCR integration and broader cancellation/crash-window acceptance remain open.
Actual ordinary owned action acceptance and held-state fault acceptance remain separate; held faults require independent qualified rescue.
automaticLockRestoration: Only after whole P5 acceptance; no settings were inspected or changed by reviewer.
